children.text: Workplace Psychology · HR Science · Organisational Behaviour
Why This Career Appeared In Your Results
3 Interested in how psychology shapes workplace behaviour and performance
3 Motivated by India's growing corporate focus on employee wellbeing and productivity
3 Enjoy combining research methods with practical business application
3 Comfortable analysing data on human behaviour at scale
3 Like influencing how organisations hire, develop, and retain people

An Industrial-Organisational (I-O) Psychologist applies psychological science to workplace issues — including hiring,
employee engagement, leadership development, team dynamics, and organisational culture — helping companies build
healthier, higher-performing workplaces through evidence-based interventions.
Applying I-O psychology to talent management and culture
Global HR consulting firms using psychometric and organisational research
Data-driven organisational psychology shaping global HR practices
Applied behavioural science for employee engagement and performance
What You Will Actually Do Day-to-Day
n Design and validate psychometric assessments for hiring and development
n Analyse employee survey and performance data to identify workplace trends
n Advise leadership on organisational culture and change management strategies
n Design training programs to improve leadership or team effectiveness
n Conduct research on employee motivation, engagement, and retention
n Present data-driven recommendations to HR and business leadership
Review employee engagement survey data and trends
Meeting with HR leadership on a talent strategy initiative

The role spans hiring science, leadership development, culture strategy,
and organisational research — assessments are one small piece

I-O psychology is a specialised, research-driven discipline requiring
rigorous training in psychological science and statistics

Startups, government bodies, and consulting firms increasingly use I-O
psychology to solve people and culture problems
Success Profile — People Who Thrive Here
Happiness Drivers — You Will Love This If...

Strong grounding in psychological research methods and
statistics · Comfortable translating data into practical business
recommendations · Skilled at influencing leadership without
formal authority · Genuinely curious about workplace
behaviour and motivation · Diplomatic in navigating
organisational politics

Seeing a data-backed intervention measurably improve
employee wellbeing or performance · Bridging rigorous science
with real business impact · Working directly with leadership on
meaningful culture change · The variety of problems — hiring,
engagement, leadership, team dynamics
n Are you interested in applying psychological science to real workplace problems?
n Are you comfortable with statistics, research methods, and data analysis?
n Can you translate research findings into practical business recommendations?
What You Will Need to Give Up

Requires balancing scientific rigor with business pragmatism
and speed · Organisational politics can slow or dilute
evidence-based recommendations · Requires continuously
proving the business value of psychological interventions ·
Demand for pure I-O roles is still emerging compared to
broader HR roles in India

Working purely as an academic researcher without business
exposure · Full autonomy over recommendations — business
priorities will shape and sometimes override your advice ·
Immediate large-scale organisational change — culture shifts
take significant time

People Often Regret This Career When: Expected the role to be purely research-focused rather than business-facing ·
Underestimated how much influence and stakeholder management the job requires · Chose it without genuine interest in
workplace psychology and organisational behaviour

Behavioural Research · Marketing Science · Consumer Insight
Why This Career Appeared In Your Results
3 Fascinated by why people buy what they buy
3 Motivated by India's booming D2C, retail, and e-commerce industries
3 Enjoy combining psychology with marketing and business strategy
3 Comfortable analysing behavioural data and consumer research
3 Like translating psychological insight into real brand and product decisions
What Is A Consumer / Shopper Psychologist?

A Consumer or Shopper Psychologist studies the mental and emotional processes behind purchasing decisions —
researching motivation, perception, and behaviour to help brands design better products, packaging, pricing, and marketing
strategies grounded in psychological science.
Large-scale consumer psychology research for FMCG brands
Global consumer research and behavioural insight firms
Applied consumer psychology in fast-growing digital-first brands
Behavioural insight informing brand strategy and campaigns
Applying shopper psychology to e-commerce experience design
What You Will Actually Do Day-to-Day
n Design and conduct consumer research studies — surveys, interviews, behavioural experiments
n Analyse purchasing data to identify psychological drivers of behaviour
n Advise brand and marketing teams on positioning, pricing, and messaging
n Conduct usability and shopper experience research in retail or digital environments
n Present behavioural insights to business and creative teams
n Stay current with behavioural economics and consumer psychology research
Review recent consumer survey or behavioural experiment data
Meeting with brand team on an upcoming product or campaign
Conduct or review consumer interviews or focus groups

Consumer psychology goes deeper into the underlying cognitive and
emotional mechanisms behind decisions, not just what people say they
want

FMCG, e-commerce, fintech, and D2C brands all employ consumer
psychologists directly in insight and strategy teams

Ethical consumer psychology focuses on genuinely understanding and
serving customer needs, not manipulation
Success Profile — People Who Thrive Here
Happiness Drivers — You Will Love This If...

Strong grounding in psychology and behavioural research
methods · Genuinely curious about human decision-making ·
Comfortable combining qualitative and quantitative research ·
Skilled at translating insight into actionable business strategy ·
Collaborative with marketing, product, and design teams

Seeing a psychological insight directly shape a successful
product or campaign · The intellectual puzzle of understanding
why people behave the way they do · Working across diverse
industries and consumer categories · Bridging rigorous science
with creative business strategy
n Are you fascinated by the psychology behind everyday consumer decisions?
n Are you comfortable combining behavioural research with business strategy?
n Can you translate psychological insight into clear, actionable recommendations?
What You Will Need to Give Up

Business pressure can sometimes prioritise speed over
rigorous research · Requires constantly balancing ethical
considerations with commercial goals · Insights can be diluted
or misapplied by non-research stakeholders · Competitive field
with growing interest from both psychologists and data
scientists

Working in a purely academic, non-commercial research
setting · Complete research autonomy — business priorities
and timelines will shape your work · Slow-paced projects —
marketing and brand cycles move quickly

People Often Regret This Career When: Expected purely academic-style research rather than fast-paced commercial work ·
Underestimated the ethical tensions between insight and persuasion · Chose it without genuine interest in psychology or
consumer behaviour

Sports Psychology · Mental Performance · Elite Athlete Support
Why This Career Appeared In Your Results
3 Fascinated by the mental side of high performance and competition
3 Motivated by India's growing investment in sports psychology post-Olympics
3 Enjoy working closely and personally with athletes and performers
3 Comfortable applying psychological science under high-pressure situations
3 Interested in performance beyond sport — music, business, the arts
What Is A Performance & Athletic Psychologist?

A Performance or Athletic Psychologist helps athletes and high performers build mental resilience, focus, and confidence —
using techniques like visualisation, goal-setting, and stress management to optimise performance under pressure and
support recovery from setbacks like injury or loss of form.
National athlete mental performance and support programs
Team psychologists supporting player mindset and performance
Elite athlete mental conditioning and support
Global benchmark in applied sports psychology support
Applying sports psychology principles to business and executive performance
What You Will Actually Do Day-to-Day
n Conduct one-on-one sessions with athletes on mental skills training
n Design and deliver visualisation, focus, and confidence-building techniques
n Support athletes through injury recovery, slumps, or high-pressure competition
n Collaborate with coaches and physiotherapists on holistic athlete development
n Conduct pre-competition mental preparation sessions
n Track and evaluate the psychological progress of athletes over time
One-on-one mental skills session with an athlete
Team meeting with coaching and medical staff

Performance psychologists increasingly work with amateur athletes,
students, performing artists, and corporate executives

Performance psychology is a specialised applied field focused on
optimisation and resilience rather than clinical diagnosis and treatment

Post-Olympic success has driven significant national investment in sports
psychology support for athletes
Success Profile — People Who Thrive Here
Happiness Drivers — You Will Love This If...

Strong foundation in psychology, particularly applied and
sports psychology · Excellent interpersonal and trust-building
skills · Calm and composed under high-pressure competitive
environments · Genuinely passionate about sport and human
performance · Patient with the emotional ups and downs of
athlete careers

Seeing an athlete overcome a mental block and perform their
best · Being trusted as part of an athlete's inner circle during
high-stakes moments · The intersection of psychology and the
excitement of competitive sport · Contributing to India's
sporting success on a national stage
n Are you fascinated by the mental and emotional side of high performance?
n Are you comfortable building deep, trust-based relationships with clients?
n Can you stay calm and supportive during high-pressure competitive situations?
What You Will Need to Give Up

Limited number of full-time roles at the elite level in India ·
Irregular hours tied to training and competition schedules,
including travel · Emotional demands of supporting athletes
through injury, loss, or career uncertainty · Requires building
trust in a field still gaining mainstream acceptance in Indian
sport

Predictable working hours — competition and training
schedules dictate availability · Purely clinical, office-based
practice — this role is highly applied and field-based ·
Immediate access to elite-level roles — most careers begin at
grassroots or academy level

People Often Regret This Career When: Expected exclusive work with top professional athletes from the start ·
Underestimated the travel and irregular hours involved · Chose it without genuine grounding in applied psychology training

Legal Psychology · Criminal Behaviour · Justice System Support
Why This Career Appeared In Your Results
3 Fascinated by the psychology behind criminal behaviour and the justice system
3 Interested in applying psychological science to legal decision-making
3 Comfortable with emotionally demanding and high-stakes casework
3 Motivated by improving India's justice and rehabilitation systems
3 Enjoy rigorous assessment, evaluation, and evidence-based reasoning

A Forensic Psychologist applies psychological expertise within the legal and criminal justice system — conducting
assessments of offenders, providing expert testimony, evaluating competency and risk, and supporting investigations,
courts, correctional facilities, and rehabilitation programs.

National Institute of Mental
Health & Neurosciences
(NIMHANS)
Forensic psychology and psychiatric assessment expertise
India's forensic science and behavioural analysis network
Supporting criminal investigations with psychological assessment
Expert witness testimony and competency evaluations
What You Will Actually Do Day-to-Day
n Conduct psychological assessments of offenders, victims, or witnesses
n Evaluate competency to stand trial and criminal responsibility
n Prepare expert reports and provide court testimony
n Assess risk of reoffending for correctional and parole decisions
n Support rehabilitation program design in correctional settings
n Collaborate with law enforcement, lawyers, and judicial officers
Review case files ahead of a scheduled assessment
Report writing for court or correctional

are the same as criminal
shows

Most work involves rigorous assessments, court reports, and rehabilitation
support rather than dramatic crime-solving

Forensic psychology applies psychological science specifically within legal
and criminal justice contexts, requiring specialised additional training

Strong foundation in clinical and legal psychology · Rigorous,

Emotionally resilient when working with difficult or disturbing

Contributing to fairer, more informed justice system decisions ·
The intellectual rigor of applying psychological science to
complex legal questions · Supporting rehabilitation that helps

Emotionally demanding exposure to trauma, violence, and

work — legal processes and evaluations often move slowly · A

trauma · Expected a more dramatic, investigation-focused role · Chose it without a genuine foundation in both psychology and
legal processes

*Ranges vary by company, city, skills, and experience. Tier-1 companies pay significantly higher.

No true fast-track exists — this field requires formal
postgraduate clinical or forensic psychology training and often
supervised practice hours. Research assistantships at forensic
psychiatry units offer valuable early exposure.
Disability Support · Recovery Psychology · Clinical Rehabilitation
Why This Career Appeared In Your Results
3 Motivated by helping people rebuild their lives after illness, injury, or disability
3 Interested in India's growing focus on disability rights and rehabilitation care
3 Enjoy long-term, relationship-based clinical work
3 Comfortable working within multidisciplinary healthcare teams
3 Find meaning in supporting resilience and adaptation

A Rehabilitation Psychologist helps individuals adapt to and recover from disability, chronic illness, or injury — providing
psychological support, coping strategies, and adjustment counselling alongside physical rehabilitation, working closely with
physiotherapists, occupational therapists, and physicians.
India's premier institute for locomotor disability rehabilitation
Hospital-based rehabilitation psychology in leading medical institutions
Specialised psychological support for spinal cord injury patients
Supporting employees recovering from illness or injury back into the workplace
What You Will Actually Do Day-to-Day
n Conduct psychological assessments for patients undergoing rehabilitation
n Provide individual and group counselling for adjustment to disability or illness
n Collaborate with physiotherapists, doctors, and occupational therapists
n Design coping and resilience-building interventions
n Support families in understanding and adapting to a loved one's condition
n Track and document patient psychological progress over time
Case review with the multidisciplinary rehabilitation team
Individual counselling session with a patient

Rehabilitation psychologists address the mental and emotional
dimensions of recovery, working alongside — not instead of — physical
therapists

The field also supports patients with chronic illness, stroke, amputation,
and neurological conditions

Growing disability rights awareness and hospital-based rehabilitation
programs are steadily increasing demand
Success Profile — People Who Thrive Here
Happiness Drivers — You Will Love This If...

Deep empathy combined with clinical rigor · Patient with
long-term, incremental recovery processes · Comfortable
working within multidisciplinary medical teams · Emotionally
resilient when supporting patients through difficult adjustment ·
Genuinely motivated by resilience and human adaptability

Watching a patient rebuild confidence and independence after
a life-changing event · Being part of a caring, collaborative
medical team · The meaningful, relationship-based nature of
long-term patient care · Contributing to a more inclusive and
disability-aware India
n Are you motivated by supporting people through significant life adjustment and recovery?
n Are you comfortable working closely within a multidisciplinary healthcare team?
n Can you sustain empathy and patience through long-term, incremental clinical work?

Emotionally demanding work supporting patients through grief
and major life adjustment · Progress can be slow and setbacks
are common · Requires close coordination with multiple
healthcare professionals · Public and family understanding of
disability psychology can still be limited in parts of India

slow and non-linear · Working in isolation — this role requires
constant coordination with medical teams · Emotional distance

People Often Regret This Career When: Underestimated the emotional demands of supporting patients through difficult
adjustment · Expected faster recovery outcomes than reality often allows · Chose it without genuine empathy-driven motivation
for clinical work

*Ranges vary by company, city, skills, and experience. Tier-1 companies pay significantly higher.
START START Rehabilitation Psychology Trainee / Assistant

B.A/B.Sc Psychology · M.A/M.Phil in Rehabilitation Psychology

Council of India (RCI)

training are required for licensed practice. Volunteering with

Wellbeing Science · Human Flourishing · Applied Positive Psychology
Why This Career Appeared In Your Results
3 Interested in what makes life meaningful, not just the absence of illness
3 Motivated by India's growing corporate and personal wellbeing movement
3 Enjoy research combined with practical, applied interventions
3 Comfortable working across clinical, corporate, and educational settings
3 Like helping people and organisations flourish, not just cope
What Is A Positive Psychologist / Wellbeing Researcher?

A Positive Psychologist or Wellbeing Researcher studies and applies the science of human flourishing — happiness,
meaning, resilience, and strengths — designing evidence-based interventions for individuals, schools, and organisations
that go beyond treating illness toward building genuine wellbeing.
Applying positive psychology to employee wellbeing strategy
India's growing academic hub for positive psychology research
Applied wellbeing science embedded in digital products
Positive education programs building student resilience
International positive psychology research and advocacy
What You Will Actually Do Day-to-Day
n Design and evaluate wellbeing interventions for individuals or organisations
n Conduct research on happiness, resilience, and human flourishing
n Facilitate workshops on strengths-based development or resilience training
n Collaborate with HR or education teams to embed wellbeing science into programs
n Analyse survey and wellbeing metric data to measure intervention impact
n Publish or present findings at wellbeing science conferences
Review wellbeing survey or intervention outcome data

Human Behaviour · Group Dynamics · Social Science Research
Why This Career Appeared In Your Results
3 Fascinated by how individuals think, feel, and behave in social contexts
3 Interested in understanding India's complex social and cultural dynamics
3 Enjoy rigorous experimental and survey-based research
3 Comfortable with both academic and applied research settings
3 Motivated by findings that can inform policy and social change
What Is A Social Psychologist / Researcher?

A Social Psychologist studies how individuals' thoughts, feelings, and behaviours are influenced by others — researching
topics like group dynamics, prejudice, persuasion, identity, and social influence — using rigorous experimental and survey
methods across academic and applied settings.
India's leading social science research institute
Leading academic centres for social psychology research
Applying social psychology to policy and public behaviour change
Global social psychology research informing development policy
Applying social psychology to online behaviour and platform design

n Design and conduct experiments or surveys studying social behaviour
n Analyse data on group dynamics, attitudes, or social influence
n Publish research findings in academic journals
n Advise policymakers or organisations on behaviourally-informed interventions
n Present research at conferences and academic or applied forums
n Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams — economists, policy researchers, technologists
Review data from a recent experiment or survey study

It is a rigorous experimental science that has produced many
counter-intuitive, well-replicated findings about human behaviour
Behavioural policy units, tech companies, and consulting firms increasingly hire social psychologists for applied research roles

Social psychology focuses more on individual cognition and behaviour
within social contexts, while sociology studies broader social structures
and institutions
Success Profile — People Who Thrive Here
Happiness Drivers — You Will Love This If...

Strong grounding in experimental design and statistics ·
Genuinely curious about human social behaviour · Comfortable
with both academic rigor and applied research settings ·
Skilled at communicating research findings clearly · Patient
with the iterative, sometimes slow pace of research

Uncovering a genuine insight into how people think and
behave in groups · Contributing research that informs better
policy or social interventions · The intellectual satisfaction of
well-designed experimental research · Working on questions
relevant to India's diverse social fabric
n Are you fascinated by how social context shapes individual thoughts and behaviour?
n Are you comfortable with rigorous experimental design and statistical analysis?
n Are you interested in research that could inform real policy or organisational change?

Academic positions are limited and competitive · Applied research roles in India are still an emerging market · Requires strong statistical and methodological rigor to produce credible findings · Research funding for pure social psychology can be limited outside major institutions

Fast career entry — meaningful research roles often require a PhD · High industry salaries seen in purely commercial fields · Guaranteed direct, immediate real-world application — much research remains foundational

A Sociologist studies human society — social institutions, relationships, culture, and structures like caste, class, gender, and
religion — using research methods ranging from large-scale surveys to in-depth ethnography, to understand and inform how
societies function and change.
India's leading independent social science research institute
India's premier institute for sociology and social work research

Crime Science · Criminal Justice Research · Policy Analysis
Why This Career Appeared In Your Results
3 Fascinated by why crime occurs and how societies respond to it
3 Motivated by improving India's criminal justice and policing systems
3 Enjoy combining sociology, psychology, and data analysis
3 Interested in evidence-based approaches to crime prevention

A Criminologist studies the causes, patterns, and prevention of crime, as well as the effectiveness of criminal justice
responses — researching topics like crime trends, policing strategy, rehabilitation, and victimology to inform evidence-based
policy and practice.
India's central body for crime data and statistics
Police reform and criminal justice research

International criminal justice research and policy support
Applied criminology informing policing and justice system reform

n Publish research in criminology or criminal justice journals
n Advise on crime prevention strategy and criminal justice reform
